records.rationale: The public checkpoint identifies a same-logical-work family, but manifestation-level and edition-specific distinctions remain unresolved. Independent bibliographic evidence sufficient for promotion has not yet been recorded in the adjudication layer.
The public checkpoint preserves multi-volume and edition-or-copy distinctions. The evidence currently recorded does not justify collapsing those distinctions into a single canonical work assertion.
Numbered-work versus aggregate distinctions remain unresolved. No canonical work identity is promoted until independent bibliography explicitly resolves the relationship.

Bardon edition and copy variants remain unresolved apart from the separately adjudicated Golden Book work identity. Publisher, year, edition statement or equivalent edition-specific evidence is not yet recorded here.
Cross-collection provenance remains unresolved. The adjudication layer does not infer work, edition or translation identity from collection alignment alone.
Shared authorship is a classification signal rather than duplicate or canonical work identity. Independent title-level bibliographic evidence is required before promotion.
